PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

Opened at 3213, measured with the CI command (`python tooling/architecture/js_ts_check.py
--count`) at HEAD on a clean detached worktree.

The unit is FILES under a `static/src` of `addons/` carrying no `// @ts-check`
in their leading comment run, after the ignore list in `eslint.config.mjs` is
applied. 852 of the 4,065 scanned files carry the directive; 3,213 do not.

Debt rather than a contract, and the argument for the floor is that the
alternative measures nothing: `tsconfig.json` sets `allowJs` with `strict`,
`noImplicitAny` and `strictNullChecks` all false, so a file without the
directive is parsed and believed and contributes zero to `tsc.json`. Deleting a
directive therefore lowers no existing floor, and adding one to a dirty file
raises `tsc` by the errors it was already hiding -- which is why this number and
`tsc` move in opposite directions and neither can stand in for the other.

Per scope on the same tree: web 2, stock 45, account 78, point_of_sale 171,
mail 397. None is zero, so none is onboarded as a hard zero yet. web`s two are
`module_loader.js` (the pre-loader IIFE, which runs before the module system)
and `service_worker.js` (measured by tsc_serviceworker against lib.webworker),
both first committed in 2023 and neither an artifact of the web_enterprise
fold.
